What is an AI website builder?

An AI website builder is a tool that creates a website from a plain-English description instead of from templates you drag and drop. You type what you want — \"a landing page for my bakery with a menu and a contact form\" — and the tool writes the actual code behind the site: the layout, the text, the styling, the structure. You keep refining it the same way, by describing changes in conversation, rather than by clicking through a page editor.

This is different from the older generation of \"drag-and-drop\" or \"template\" website builders. Those tools give you a fixed set of blocks and layouts to arrange by hand. An AI website builder instead reads your description, decides on a structure, and generates new code to match it — closer to how a developer would build the site, just automated and driven by natural language.

A plain-language analogy

Think of the difference between ordering from a fixed menu and telling a chef what you're in the mood for. A template builder is the fixed menu: pick a layout, swap the photos and colors, and you're limited to what's on the menu. An AI website builder is closer to describing the meal you want and having it prepared to order — you say what you're after, and the result is built specifically for that request rather than pulled from a preset list.

Why it matters

The practical effect is who gets to build a website at all, and how fast. A few things change:

  • No coding required to start. Describing a page in a sentence replaces the need to learn HTML, CSS, or a page-builder's own interface.
  • Faster first draft. A working page can exist in minutes instead of hours of assembling sections and adjusting spacing by hand.
  • Iteration by conversation. Instead of hunting through menus to change a headline or add a section, you just say what you want changed.
  • Lower stakes for experimenting. Because generating and adjusting a page is fast and cheap, it's easier to try an idea, see it rendered, and change direction.

This matters most for people who have a clear idea of what they want but no interest in — or budget for — learning a page builder or hiring a developer for a first version: solo founders, small businesses, students, and anyone testing an idea before investing more time in it.

A real example: from sentence to live site

Here's what the process typically looks like in practice:

  1. You open a chat interface and type something like: \"Build a one-page site for a freelance photographer, with a hero section, a portfolio grid, and a contact section.\"
  2. The tool generates a real, working page matching that description — actual layout, actual text, actual styling — and shows you a live preview of it.
  3. You look at the preview and describe a change: \"Make the hero darker and move the contact section above the portfolio.\" The tool updates the page to match.
  4. Once you're happy with it, you publish it with one click and it's live at a public URL anyone can visit.

No dragging boxes around a canvas, no picking from a locked set of section templates — just describing what you want and watching it get built.

How Kodely handles it

Kodely is an AI website builder built around exactly this chat-based workflow, with a few specifics worth knowing:

  • Real code, not a template. When you describe a site, Kodely generates an actual Vite + React 19 + TypeScript + Tailwind CSS v4 application — real component files built on hand-built UI primitives, not a theme with your text dropped in.
  • Live preview as you go. The preview you see is the actual compiled app being built, not a mockup of it.
  • Changes stay conversational. To adjust anything, you describe the change in chat and Kodely edits the real underlying components.
  • Free checkpoints. Every version is saved, and rolling back to an earlier one is free if a change doesn't work out.
  • Code view. You can see and copy the generated source directly in the app.
  • One-click publish. Your site goes live at a free yourname.kodely.site URL, included with every project.

Worth being clear about what Kodely doesn't do yet: it's a frontend builder, so it doesn't currently generate backends, databases, authentication, or payment systems, and it doesn't offer custom domains, code export, or click-to-edit visual editing — changes go through chat. It's focused on turning a description into a real, working frontend fast, and building on that well.

Related terms

If you're new to this space, it's also worth reading What is vibe coding? — the broader practice of building software by describing intent in natural language, of which AI website building is one specific application.

Try it yourself

The easiest way to understand an AI website builder is to use one. Kodely gives new accounts 750 free credits with no card required, enough to generate and publish a first site. You can sign up and describe your first page in a sentence, check the pricing if you want to see what happens after the free credits, or browse the blog for more guides like this one. If you already have an account, you can log in and pick up where you left off." }

Here's what that means, a real example, and how Kodely builds actual React apps.", "targetKeyword": "what is an ai website builder", "category": "Glossary", "bodyHtml": "

What is an AI website builder?

An AI website builder is a tool that creates a website from a plain-English description instead of from templates you drag and drop. You type what you want — \"a landing page for my bakery with a menu and a contact form\" — and the tool writes the actual code behind the site: the layout, the text, the styling, the structure. You keep refining it the same way, by describing changes in conversation, rather than by clicking through a page editor.

This is different from the older generation of \"drag-and-drop\" or \"template\" website builders. Those tools give you a fixed set of blocks and layouts to arrange by hand. An AI website builder instead reads your description, decides on a structure, and generates new code to match it — closer to how a developer would build the site, just automated and driven by natural language.

A plain-language analogy

Think of the difference between ordering from a fixed menu and telling a chef what you're in the mood for. A template builder is the fixed menu: pick a layout, swap the photos and colors, and you're limited to what's on the menu. An AI website builder is closer to describing the meal you want and having it prepared to order — you say what you're after, and the result is built specifically for that request rather than pulled from a preset list.

Why it matters

The practical effect is who gets to build a website at all, and how fast. A few things change:

  • No coding required to start. Describing a page in a sentence replaces the need to learn HTML, CSS, or a page-builder's own interface.
  • Faster first draft. A working page can exist in minutes instead of hours of assembling sections and adjusting spacing by hand.
  • Iteration by conversation. Instead of hunting through menus to change a headline or add a section, you just say what you want changed.
  • Lower stakes for experimenting. Because generating and adjusting a page is fast and cheap, it's easier to try an idea, see it rendered, and change direction.

This matters most for people who have a clear idea of what they want but no interest in — or budget for — learning a page builder or hiring a developer for a first version: solo founders, small businesses, students, and anyone testing an idea before investing more time in it.

A real example: from sentence to live site

Here's what the process typically looks like in practice:

  1. You open a chat interface and type something like: \"Build a one-page site for a freelance photographer, with a hero section, a portfolio grid, and a contact section.\"
  2. The tool generates a real, working page matching that description — actual layout, actual text, actual styling — and shows you a live preview of it.
  3. You look at the preview and describe a change: \"Make the hero darker and move the contact section above the portfolio.\" The tool updates the page to match.
  4. Once you're happy with it, you publish it with one click and it's live at a public URL anyone can visit.

No dragging boxes around a canvas, no picking from a locked set of section templates — just describing what you want and watching it get built.

How Kodely handles it

Kodely is an AI website builder built around exactly this chat-based workflow, with a few specifics worth knowing:

  • Real code, not a template. When you describe a site, Kodely generates an actual Vite + React 19 + TypeScript + Tailwind CSS v4 application — real component files built on hand-built UI primitives, not a theme with your text dropped in.
  • Live preview as you go. The preview you see is the actual compiled app being built, not a mockup of it.
  • Changes stay conversational. To adjust anything, you describe the change in chat and Kodely edits the real underlying components.
  • Free checkpoints. Every version is saved, and rolling back to an earlier one is free if a change doesn't work out.
  • Code view. You can see and copy the generated source directly in the app.
  • One-click publish. Your site goes live at a free yourname.kodely.site URL, included with every project.

Worth being clear about what Kodely doesn't do yet: it's a frontend builder, so it doesn't currently generate backends, databases, authentication, or payment systems, and it doesn't offer custom domains, code export, or click-to-edit visual editing — changes go through chat. It's focused on turning a description into a real, working frontend fast, and building on that well.
